# CT trauma: Dr Fiona Rennie (fictional)

Dr Rennie is a consultant emergency and trauma radiologist at a fictional major trauma centre. Her reports are terse and organised by region. There is an inline `Clinical details:` line giving the mechanism and physiology, a fixed `Technique:` line, and regional paragraph headers (`Head:`, `Cervical spine:`, `Chest:` and so on) on whole-body studies. Limited head and cervical spine studies drop those headers and use a shorter technique line.
She writes pertinent negatives as short stock sentences and grades solid organ injuries as "AAST grade". She says "active extravasation" and calls uninjured organs "unremarkable".
Her conclusion is a numbered list with the most serious injury first. It closes with "No other acute traumatic injury." and the line "Preliminary findings relayed to the trauma team leader in CT at {time}."
